definitions.explanation: The degree of difficulty of a task, test, game, or challenge — especially one that can be rated or compared on a scale.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{試験|しけん}は{難易度|なんいど}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: This exam has a high difficulty level.

examples.japanese: このゲームは{難易度|なんいど}を{選|えら}べる。
examples.english: In this game you can choose the difficulty level.

examples.japanese: {昨年|さくねん}に{比|くら}べて{問題|もんだい}の{難易度|なんいど}が{上|あ}がったと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Compared to last year, the difficulty of the questions is said to have gone up.

notes:
Compound of {難|なん} (difficult) + {易|い} (easy) + {度|ど} (degree). Functions as a measurement noun — high values mean more difficult.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {難易度|なんいど}が{高|たか}い / {低|ひく}い: high / low difficulty
- {難易度|なんいど}{設定|せってい}: difficulty setting
- {難易度|なんいど}が{上|あ}がる / {下|さ}がる: difficulty rises / falls
- {難易度|なんいど}{別|べつ}: by difficulty level

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {難|むずか}しさ: difficulty (general feeling) — {難易度|なんいど} is measured/rated; {難|むずか}しさ is more subjective
- レベル: level — overlaps for games but lacks the difficult/easy axis built into {難易度|なんいど}
